title: shrink+symmetry GW gives bad bands and an unfinished LibRPA job because the direct-ABF atom-pair set is not closed under star-group rotations
symptom: shrink+symmetry GW runs produced very bad band figures and the full LibRPA job could not finish (missing blocks). Nothing was obviously wrong earlier in the chain: the chi0 projection error was only 1e-8 to 1e-7 and the V/W_c differences about one percent; the amplification appeared later in the W_c(R,tau)/Sigma_c assembly in strongly cancelling channels.
root_cause: In the direct-ABF path the intermediate atom-pair set was not closed under star-group rotations, so the source atom-pair blocks required by rotation were missing and a q point could not be assembled from all upper-triangle pair blocks.
minimal_fix: Generate and expect a source atom-pair set closed under the star-group rotations (add the rotation-required source atom-pair blocks) so every q point yields all upper-triangle pair blocks, and make the reader fail loudly on metadata mismatch, duplicate block or missing block instead of continuing silently.
validation: The full LibRPA job completes after the closure fix; then check matrix completeness, Hermiticity/PSD, k-star correspondence and the near-gap cross-spin mirror before comparing bands. Execution-level success alone is not a physics result.
avoid: Do not treat 'the job finishes' as physics validation. Do not attribute the no-shrink/no-sym versus shrink/sym GW gap difference to shrink or symmetry - those runs also changed the ABFS and the binary (1.57345 eV vs 1.60117 eV, 27.7 meV, cannot be assigned to a single factor). Do not re-enable shrink before EXX itself passes.

parameters.pair_block_rule: every q point must receive all upper-triangle atom-pair blocks, with the source atom-pair set closed under star-group rotations
parameters.reader_behaviour: fail on metadata mismatch, duplicate block, missing block, illegal offset
parameters.reintroduce_shrink_after: no-shrink EXX passes the four-corner check (full-q/sym-off, IBZ/sym-on, Ewald full-Coulomb, direct-G Coulomb)
